bull.b: The combination of low-20s sales growth and margins at or above 65% indicates that On is scaling without sacrificing premium economics. If sustained, this supports stronger earnings compounding, greater reinvestment in products and stores, and improved resilience across its global business.

Rapid DTC growth gives On greater control over pricing, presentation, customer data and brand experience than wholesale distribution alone. A rising DTC mix can support higher-quality revenue, improve long-term customer relationships and reduce reliance on third-party retail partners.

A net cash position and substantial free cash flow provide financial flexibility to fund product innovation, retail expansion and international growth internally. This also gives On capacity to absorb operating volatility while preserving strategic options and supporting future capital returns.

bear.b: Slower wholesale growth and promotional pressure can weaken sell-through, reduce channel productivity and make revenue timing less predictable. Continued softness would require careful partner and inventory management, while limiting the contribution of a major route to market during the next several months.

A much larger inventory base increases the need for disciplined forecasting and sell-through management, particularly while wholesale sell-in is being calibrated. If demand or channel timing disappoints, excess stock could pressure working capital, promotions or gross-margin quality even if management cites volume growth.

Higher import tariffs can create ongoing pressure on product costs and profitability in the U.S. market, while the timing of refunds makes the benefit difficult to forecast. This uncertainty complicates margin planning and could offset part of the operating leverage expected from growth and mix.
